title: I'm Standing on a Million Lives
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ninth grader Yusuke Yotsuya and two classmates are pulled into a game-like other world by a half-faced Game Master who sets timed quests; dead players respawn only if one of them survives. More players join over time, they return to ordinary life between quests, and the worlds they visit age while they do not. Yotsuya, a misanthropic loner, is pushed toward helping others because it is the only path to survival.
life_message: Even a self-declared loner who scorns people finds that survival, and meaning, require working for others.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are survival quests, not personal honor disputes.

Order vs freedom.evidence: The Game Master's rules and time limits govern everything.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Bonds are with party members and NPCs, not family.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Class and level systems, but party members are peers.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival is the hero's stated priority (Wikipedia).

folkways.japan: Yotsuya's withdrawal from classmates and clubs reflects Japanese concern with social isolation among youth, set against the group harmony a party requires.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer calls it a misguided attempt to subvert isekai with no clear thematic endpoint; Wikipedia shows the lesson forced by quest rules.

personified.ideology: Selfish pragmatism and misanthropy; survival over social norms

delivery.note: The hero's cynical worldview is voiced openly and is gradually tested by the quests' design rather than refuted by a speech.

winners_losers: Cooperation wins quests; Yotsuya's misanthropy is given sympathy as a wounded stance but shown as unworkable alone.
